account: It is ten in the morning, and I am outside town hall, about to begin my scheduled market walk. So far I have no firm evidence of anything unusual happening. Townsfolk 08 and 28 both said the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery; that sounds like ordinary bread-making supplies, not evidence of a secret undertaking. Several townsfolk are gathered near the hall and market, and I saw the builder walking with a lantern, but I do not know their purposes. The secretary reports no correspondence or town news yet. My afternoon tea appointment is oddly vague: the book says only 'the neighbour, dockside cottage (east bank),' and neither I nor the secretary knows the host's name or exact cottage. I have asked the secretary to verify the address before my one o'clock accounts appointment. That may simply be incomplete scheduling rather than anything concealed. I still feel I should learn more about local affairs, but I cannot yet identify any hidden plan or its participants.
